rejected.title: Threats to coastal environments
card: Coasts are always changing, but people can speed up the change or make its effects worse. A threat is anything that damages a coastal environment or puts it at risk.
Building and dunes

Houses, roads and car parks built close to the shore leave beaches no room to move. Walking across dunes and clearing dune plants removes the roots that hold sand in place, so wind and waves can wear the dunes away.
Sea level and storms
Rising sea levels put the water line higher up the shore, so waves reach further inland. Storm waves can strip sand from a beach in a few hours and cut into dunes and cliffs.
Pollution
Litter, oil and runoff from streets and farms wash into coastal waters. This can harm marine life, such as fish and seabirds, and make beaches unsafe for swimming.
rejected.remember: Threats to coasts come from people and from nature, and building, storms and rising seas can add to each other.

a.q: A council lets people walk across a dune, and the dune plants die. Why does this threaten the beach?
opts: Without roots to hold it, wind and waves can move the sand
Plant leaves make the sea level rise on that beach
Dead plants make storm waves form further out at sea
Dead plants make the water too polluted to swim in
a.why: Dune plant roots bind the sand together. Without them, wind and waves can carry the sand away. Pollution is a different threat, and it is not the result of plants dying.
a.clue: Think about what plant roots do to loose sand.

b.q: Houses are built right behind the dunes at a beach in Port Macquarie. A severe storm then strikes. Why are these houses at greater risk?
opts: The beach has no room to move back, so waves reach them
The storm waves are larger because houses are near the shore
The houses cause the sea level to rise around them
The houses make the sand wash in from the open sea
b.why: Building close to the shore leaves a beach with no space to move, and storm waves can cut into the dunes and reach the houses. The houses do not make waves larger or raise the sea level. They only put people and property in the way of the waves.
b.clue: Ask what the beach needs room to do.

version.remember: Building near the shore, lost dune plants, rising seas, storms and pollution can each damage a coast or put it at risk.
